segments.label: Launch & ascent — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A
segments.note: SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A (28.608°, -80.604°); ~9 min analytic ascent to a 185 km parking orbit (schematic arc, real pad and launch time).

segments.label: Parking orbit coast
segments.note: Circular 185 km parking orbit, inclination 28.6° (plane through the pad at launch and the Moon at arrival — the launch-window geometry). Coast 177 min to the injection burn into the phasing ellipse.

segments.label: Earth-orbit phasing loops
segments.note: Highly elliptical Earth orbits with apogee-raising burns at perigee (burn dates published by the provider; apogee values are modeled). The final loop is stretched so the last perigee passage coincides with the TLI time.

segments.label: Trans-lunar coast (5.5 days)
segments.note: Two-body Lambert arc from the TLI point to the modeled LOI point (Moon's position from the ephemeris at LOI). Departure Δv 73 m/s, arrival v∞ 0.80 km/s. Mid-course corrections not modeled.

segments.label: Lunar orbit (100 km)
segments.note: Circular orbit after LOI; the landing site has not been published, so no descent is drawn.

events.title: Launch — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A · SpaceX Falcon 9

notes: Projected route: the provider's previous flight profile applied to the announced window; dates are illustrative until the launch is scheduled.

Blue Ghost Mission 2 (far side, with ESA's Lunar Pathfinder relay) is NET late 2026. Route projected from Mission 1's profile (≈25 days of Earth-orbit phasing, ~5-day transit, ~16 days in lunar orbit) on an illustrative date; the far-side landing coordinates are not yet published, so the route ends in lunar orbit.

Injection burn placed at 2026-11-10T09:05:57Z (published/nominal 2026-11-10T07:00:00Z): the perigee of the phasing ellipse is put where the final departure toward the Moon is tangential (apsidal drift over the phasing weeks is not modeled).
